articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Administrative Associate, G-6, Temporary Appointment, 364 days, #00138510, Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, APR Apply now Job no: 595939 Contract type: Temporary Appointment Duty Station: Cox's Bazaar Level: G-6 Location: Bangladesh Categories: Administration UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to Dedication The fundamental mission of UNICEF is to promote the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything the organization does — in programs, in advocacy and in operations. The equity strategy, emphasizing the most disadvantaged and excluded children and families, translates this commitment to children’s rights into action. For UNICEF, equity means that all children have an opportunity to survive, develop and reach their full potential, without discrimination, bias or favoritism. To the degree that any child has an unequal chance in life — in its social, political, economic, civic and cultural dimensions — her or his rights are violated. There is growing evidence that investing in the health, education and protection of a society’s most disadvantaged citizens — addressing inequity — not only will give all children the opportunity to fulfill their potential but also will lead to sustained growth and stability of countries. This is why the focus on equity is so vital. It accelerates progress towards realizing the human rights of all children, which is the universal mandate of UNICEF, as outlined by the Convention on the Rights of the Child, while also supporting the equitable development of nations. Under the supervision and guidance of the Administrative Officer NOA, the incumbent is responsible for executing a broad variety of general service tasks including travel and event logistics, receiving and dispatching mail, as well as some specialized tasks related to the office fleet management, inspection and maintenance of electro-mechanical equipment and infrastructure of all UNICEF Cox’s Bazar facilities, including main office, warehouse and compound infrastructure. For effective performance of duties under this post, the incumbent will be required to have thorough knowledge of UNICEF/UN administrative procedures, processes and policies. Major duties and responsibilities: Office vehicle fleet management Electro-mechanical systems management Booking Hotel accommodation for official visitors Receiving invoices from vendors and implementing partners and coordinate office courier and mail distribution Payment and Invoice Processing If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Temporary Appointment ToR_Administrative Associate, GS-6, TA, CXB_FINAL VA (2).pdf To qualify as a champion for every child you will have… Education : Completion of secondary education is required. Work Experience : A minimum of six (6) years of professional experience in office management, administration, finance, accounting, ICT, human resources, supply or any other relevant function. A bachelor’s degree from a recognized academic institution in a field relevant to the position may replace three years of related work experience. A master’s degree may replace an additional two years. Skills : Electromechanical, Electromechanical Engineering, Power Supply, Routine Inspections, Drive to Achieve, Manages Ambiguity. Language Requirements : Fluency in English is required. Electromechanical engineering coursework, electrical inspections experience, solar power systems experience, generator operations experience, HVAC systems experience, fire detection systems experience, renewable energy, international organization experience, electrical documentation proficiency, forklift operations knowledge Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. Supplemental technical or university courses related to the field of Electrical/Mechanical/Electromechanical Engineering is added advantage. Knowledge and professional expertise needed to conduct routine inspections of electrical layout of large office facilities, power supply systems, including solar and generator, cleaning the solar panels, and ability to address any technical issues that may arise will be considered a very strong asset. Expertise to ensure the uninterrupted operation of the office and the safety of all occupants by adhering to electromechanical codes and regulations is desirable. Relevant experience in a UN system agency or organization is considered as an asset. Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) or a local language For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidate’s willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is an equal-opportunity employer, we actively encourage applications from female candidates, gender-diverse individuals and people with disabilities. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. UNICEF staff members holding fixed-term, continuing, or permanent appointments who are considered to be on abolished post status may apply for this temporary position and, if selected with a start date before 31 December 2025, may take it up as a temporary assignment, in line with UNICEF guidance on separation due to the abolition of posts or staff reductions. They will retain their fixed-term entitlements but will not hold a lien to their abolished post. For other scenarios where a Temporary Assignment may be possible, please refer to Additional guidance on IP to IP temporary assignments after completion of the full TOD.pdf (accessible to UNICEF personnel only). The conditions of a temporary assignment, including relocation entitlements, will depend on the status of the staff member’s original appointment and may be limited in accordance with applicable UNICEF policies, procedures, and practices in force. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Visa residence requirements: i.e. UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of visa and working authorization for candidates under consideration for positions at the national officer and general service category. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. You must agree to the privacy statement 🚀 Shape the future of Operations at UNICEF Bangladesh. UNICEF Bangladesh is seeking a qualified and motivated professional for the position of Administrative Associate, based in Cox’s Bazar. The position will support the effective delivery of administrative services, including office and facilities management, travel, fleet coordination, procurement support, contract monitoring, and other operational requirements of the Field Office. As the GS-6 Administrative Associate in UNICEF’s Cox’s Bazar Field Office, you will be a key member of the Operations team, providing essential administrative and operational support for the timely delivery of UNICEF’s programmes. Working under the supervision and guidance of the Administrative Officer, you will support administrative coordination, travel and mission management, office operations, protocol services, and liaison with the Bangladesh Country Office in Dhaka. You will collaborate closely with programme and operations colleagues, UN agencies, government counterparts, partners, service providers, and other stakeholders. Location: Bangladesh Deadline: 5 Oct 2026 11:55 PM

The purpose of the consultancy is to strengthen OIAI’s data analytics and business intelligence capabilities by developing a semi-automated or automated and sustainable approach to assurance mapping and related audit analytics. The assignment will focus on enhancing the existing assurance mapping model and developing a dynamic analytical solution, preferably using Power BI or similar technology, to facilitate the integration, analysis, visualization and updating of assurance coverage data. The consultancy will also develop analytical tools and outputs that can be applied to related OIAI processes, including the audit universe, risk assessment, audit planning and annual reporting. The assignment is temporary and output-based, with defined analytical products, milestones and knowledge-transfer deliverables to be completed within the consultancy period. The consultant will support further development of OIAI’s assurance mapping and related audit analytics. The work will include maintaining and enhancing the existing Excel-based assurance map; consolidating and integrating relevant assurance and audit data; developing a more automated and dynamic solution, preferably in Power BI or similar technology; and producing analytical tools and visualizations to support assurance mapping, the audit universe, risk assessment, planning and reporting. The assignment will also include testing, documenting and supporting the handover of the developed solutions. At least two years of relevant work experience in data analytics, data management, business intelligence, data visualization, analytical research or other related areas. Relevant experience may include internships, academic projects or other practical assignments involving data extraction, structuring, analysis and presentation. Strong proficiency in Excel and Power BI or similar business intelligence/data visualization tools; experience in cleaning, structuring and integrating data from multiple sources; ability to develop dashboards and automated analytical solutions; strong analytical and problem-solving skills; and ability to document analytical processes and present data clearly to non-technical users. articles.seo_title: تعلن Orange Business عن فرصة توظيف محلل أمن سيبراني مبتدئ بالدار البيضاء
articles.seo_description: تعلن Orange Business عن فرصة توظيف محلل أمن سيبراني مبتدئ بالدار البيضاء. المهام تشمل إدارة تنبيهات الأمن وتحليل الحوادث. التقديم متاح الآن.
articles.final_html:
تعلن شركة Orange Business بالمغرب عن فرصة توظيف لمنصب محلل أمن سيبراني مبتدئ (Analyste Cybersécurité Junior) بمدينة الدار البيضاء. هذه الفرصة موجهة للشغوفين بالأمن الرقمي والراغبين في تطوير مسيرتهم المهنية ضمن بيئة عمل محفزة وديناميكية في مجال الأمن السيبراني.

تفاصيل الوظيفة

المؤسسة Orange Business
المنصب محلل أمن سيبراني مبتدئ (Analyste Cybersécurité Junior)
الموقع الدار البيضاء، المغرب
نوع العقد عقد عمل دائم (CDI)
نظام العمل دوام كامل
تاريخ النشر 29 سبتمبر 2026
المرجع ICM-589088

المهام والمسؤوليات

  • مراقبة وإدارة تنبيهات الأمن السيبراني بفعالية.
  • تحليل معمق للحوادث الأمنية وتحديد مسبباتها وسبل معالجتها.
  • المساهمة بفاعلية في تطوير وتحسين العمليات والإجراءات الأمنية القائمة.

الشروط والمؤهلات

  • إظهار شغف كبير ومستمر بمجال الأمن الرقمي والسيبراني.
  • القدرة على التعلم والتطور في بيئة عمل سريعة الوتيرة، وامتلاك أساسيات المعرفة بمجال الأمن السيبراني (مستوى مبتدئ).

التقديم والروابط الرسمية

على المرشحين المهتمين والذين يستوفون الشروط المحددة، تقديم طلباتهم مباشرة من خلال الرابط الإلكتروني الرسمي المخصص للتوظيف:

articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Senior Communication Associate (Writer & Editor) (G-7), Fixed Term, #00134069, Global Communication and Advocacy, ICSE - Budapest, Hungary Apply now Job no: 595952 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: Budapest Level: G-7 Location: Hungary Categories: Communication UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to be heard Internal Communication and Staff Engagement (ICSE) is a strategic organizational enabler that supports staff engagement, organizational alignment, and culture across UNICEF's global workforce. As UNICEF continues to evolve in a changing global environment, effective internal communication plays an essential role in strengthening connection to UNICEF's mission and values, supporting organizational priorities, and fostering trust across the workforce. The position is located within the Global Internal Communication and Staff Engagement (ICSE) section of the Division of Global Communication and Advocacy (DGCA). The ICSE team leads the development and implementation of global internal communication strategies, channels, campaigns, and engagement initiatives that inform, connect, and engage UNICEF personnel worldwide. It also serves as a coordination, guidance, and support hub for internal communication across Headquarters, Regional Offices, and Country Offices. How can you make a difference? The Senior Communication Associate (Writer & Editor) serves as the principal writer and editor within UNICEF's Global ICSE team. The role is responsible for developing high-quality organizational communications, stories and other editorial content that help personnel stay informed about UNICEF's priorities, initiatives, organizational developments, and impact. The role identifies content opportunities, researches complex topics, and develops clear, accurate and engaging communications informed by diverse perspectives and sources. Through strong writing, editing, and storytelling, the incumbent translates complex organizational information into accessible content that informs, engages, and connects UNICEF personnel worldwide. Key functions and related duties: 1. Organizational Communications, Writing and Editorial Content Development Write, edit and produce high-quality organizational communications, strategic updates, stories, feature articles, interviews, and other editorial content for global internal audiences. Develop content that supports awareness and understanding of UNICEF's strategic priorities, key initiatives, organizational developments and matters of institutional importance. Research complex topics, gather and synthesize information from multiple sources, and translate it into clear, accurate, and engaging communications for diverse internal audiences. Identify content opportunities, develop compelling and strategic story angles, and produce timely content related to organizational priorities and developments affecting UNICEF's work. Conduct interviews and stakeholder engagement to support content development and storytelling. Exercise sound editorial judgment to ensure content is strategic, relevant, audience-focused and aligned with internal communication objectives. Ensure factual accuracy, editorial quality and alignment with internal communication standards, editorial guidelines and UNICEF values. 2. Content Publishing and Editorial Production Publish and distribute content across UNICEF's internal communication channels, including ICON, SharePoint, Outlook, Viva Amplify, Viva Engage, Teams and other key platforms. Create, format and maintain SharePoint pages and other digital content assets for stories, organizational messages, announcements, and campaign content. Manage uMessage, including coordinating, drafting and distributing organizational messages in collaboration with relevant stakeholders. Maintain ICON, UNICEF's intranet homepage, and related internal communication products, ensuring content remains timely, accurate and engaging. Coordinate content publication schedules and related publishing activities across channels. Support lock-screen communications and related publishing processes. Ensure published content complies with accessibility, usability and brand standards. 3. Contributor Engagement, Editorial Guidance and Standards Build and maintain productive relationships with communication focal points, contributors and stakeholders across UNICEF. Identify content opportunities and work with contributors across the organization to source, develop, and strengthen content for global internal audiences. Review and edit submissions to improve clarity, structure, storytelling, audience relevance, and alignment with editorial standards. Provide guidance and practical support to colleagues and contributors developing content for internal communication channels. Help identify and amplify compelling stories, innovations, lessons learned and good practices from across the organization. Contribute to the development and application of editorial guidance, standards, templates and tools that support content quality and consistency. Support knowledge-sharing and capacity-building initiatives related to internal writing, editing, and storytelling. 4. Monitoring, Reporting and Continuous Improvement Monitor content performance and audience engagement using available analytics tools. Provide periodic reports and recommendations that support continuous improvement of internal communication products and approaches. Assess audience engagement trends and contribute insights to improve content quality, relevance, and effectiveness. Support the application of editorial and publishing standards and identify opportunities to strengthen content quality and consistency. Support coordination with Operations and other relevant business units as required. Support procurement and administrative processes, including the processing of purchase orders and invoices. Provide periodic updates on administrative and budget-related matters, as required. Provide administrative support to the ICSE team. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Senior Communication Associate (Writer & Editor), GS7-ICSE.pdf To qualify as a champion for every child you will have… Education : Completion of secondary education is required. A Bachelor or equivalent (First Level University Degree) from a recognized academic institution in a field relevant to the position may replace 3 years of related work experience. A Master or equivalent (Advanced University Degree) may replace an additional 2 years. Work Experience : A minimum of 7 years of progressively responsible professional experience in journalism, writing, editing, publishing, communications, digital media, or a related field is required. Demonstrated experience researching, gathering and synthesizing information from multiple sources, and developing, writing and editing stories, features, interviews and other editorial content for diverse audiences is essential. Proven ability to manage multiple assignments and deliver high-quality content within demanding timelines is essential. Experience working with contributors, subject-matter experts and stakeholders to develop and curate content is essential. Skills : Exceptional writing and editing skills in English, including the ability to develop and review organizational communications and editorial content. Strong editorial judgment and news sense, including the ability to identify organizational priorities, audience-relevant stories, key messages and effective storytelling approaches. Strong interviewing, research, and fact-checking skills. Ability to translate complex information into clear, accurate, and engaging content. Ability to work effectively under pressure and manage competing priorities while maintaining high standards of quality and accuracy. Proficiency in Microsoft 365 tools, including SharePoint, Viva Engage, and Viva Amplify. Language Requirements: Fluency and excellent command of written and spoken English is required. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) is an asset. A university degree (Bachelor's or higher) in Journalism, English, Communications, Media Studies, Digital Media, International Relations or another relevant field is an asset. Specialized training or coursework in writing, editing, journalism, storytelling, digital publishing, multimedia content production or related fields is an asset. Demonstrated experience writing and editing high-quality organizational communications, strategic updates, leadership messages or other communications for internal or professional audiences is highly desirable. Experience publishing content through digital channels, content management systems, or internal communication platforms is desirable. Experience using content analytics, reporting, or audience insights to support content improvement is desirable. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable applicants are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Visa residence requirements: i.e. UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of a visa and working authorization for candidates under consideration for positions at the national officer and general service category. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Provide periodic reports and recommendations that support continuous improvement of internal communication products and approaches. Assess audience engagement trends and contribute insights to improve content quality, relevance, and effectiveness. Support the application of editorial and publishing standards and identify opportunities to strengthen content quality and consistency. Proven ability to manage multiple assignments and deliver high-quality content within demanding timelines is essential. Experience working with contributors, subject-matter experts and stakeholders to develop and curate content is essential. Strong editorial judgment and news sense, including the ability to identify organizational priorities, audience-relevant stories, key messages and effective storytelling approaches. Proficiency in Microsoft 365 tools, including SharePoint, Viva Engage, and Viva Amplify. Language Requirements: Fluency and excellent command of written and spoken English is required. articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Social Policy Specialist (Development) (NO-3), TA (364 days), #00138378, Quetta - Pakistan, APR (Open to nationals of Pakistan only) Apply now Job no: JPR0004191 Contract type: Temporary Appointment Duty Station: Quetta Location: Pakistan Categories: Social Policy UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to a Hero How can you make a difference? The Social Policy Specialist (Development), NO-C, is based in the UNICEF Field Office in Quetta and reports to the Chief Field Office, P-5, with technical guidance from the Chief of Social Policy The role of the Social Policy Specialist (Development) is to support UNICEF field office Quetta to have an analytical and evidence-based understanding of the political, social, cultural, political economy and overall development context in the province which affect the programming environment, to help UNICEF to position itself to advance the rights of children. Under the general guidance of the Chief Field Office and technical guidance of the Chief Social Policy, the incumbent is responsible for providing technical support to the implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of all stages of social policy programme and related advocacy from strategic planning and formulation to delivery of concrete and sustainable results, as well as lead the gender but also disability mainstreaming/ programming. Analysis of the development context and emerging development issues in the province to position UNICEF in the advancement of children's rights. Improving use of public financial resources for children. Strengthening social protection coverage and impact for children. Improving data on child poverty & vulnerability for increased use for policy and programme action Strengthened advocacy and partnerships for child-sensitive social policy. Lead the Gender Equality Agenda Support to the Evaluation and Research function at PCO If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: JD_Social Policy and Development Specialist Quetta.pdf To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have… Education : Master or equivalent (Advanced University Degree) in Economics, International Development, Political Science, Social Science, Social Policy, Public Policy, International Relations, Socio-Economic Development, or a related field is required. Work Experience : A minimum of five years of relevant professional work experience in social policy, social protection, child poverty, public finance, governance, policy analysis, programme planning or another related area is required. Solid understanding of the development context in Pakistan, including the country's decentralized governance structure is a requirement. Skills : Stakeholder Coordination, Humanitarian Engagement, Process Expertise, Effective Communication, Policy Writing, Information Dissemination. Language Requirements : English - Proficient/Fluent is required. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) or a local language is considered an asset. Developing country experience and/or emergency response experience will be an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts is desirable. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) or a local language is considered an asset. Developing country experience and/or emergency response experience will be an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts is desirable. For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female candidates, persons with disabilities and suitable candidates from underrepresented groups are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Visa residence requirements: i.e. UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of a visa and working authorization for candidates under consideration for positions at the national officer and general service category. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Resumen de funciones/responsabilidades clave: Almacenamiento y gestión de inventarios Mecanismos alternativos de entrega y servicios de adquisiciones Otras funciones/responsabilidades Si deseas obtener más información sobre esta posición, por favor revisa la descripción completa del puesto aquí: Supply Logistics Assistant G-5.pdf Para ser un/a defensor/a de los derechos de la niñez, deberás contar con… Educación: Se requiere educación secundaria completada. Un título universitario de primer nivel (licenciatura/grado) completado, obtenido en una institución académica reconocida y en un campo relevante para el puesto, puede sustituir (3) tres años de experiencia laboral relacionada. Un título de maestría completado puede sustituir dos (2) años adicionales de experiencia. Experiencia laboral: Se requiere un mínimo de cinco años de experiencia administrativa pertinente en gestión de la cadena de suministro o en un entorno comercial. Un título universitario de primer nivel (licenciatura/grado) completado, obtenido en una institución académica reconocida y en un campo relevante para el puesto, por ejemplo, cadena de suministro, administración de empresas, derecho contractual/comercial, ingenieria industrial o areas afines. Habilidades : Capacidad para gestionar proveedores y realizar seguimiento de su desempeño. Habilidad para realizar el seguimiento de envíos y coordinar las entregas oportunamente. Capacidad para realizar pronósticos de suministros y anticipar necesidades de abastecimiento. Habilidad para analizar datos y generar información relevante para la toma de decisiones. Experiencia en la gestión y coordinación de operaciones de almacén. Idiomas: se requiere nivel avanzado de español. Idiomas: El conocimiento de ingles intermedio es deseable. Se considera una ventaja la comprensión del trabajo de desarrollo y acción humanitaria. Se considera una ventaja contar con conocimientos prácticos de ERP/SAP. Se considera deseable contar con experiencia en gestión de la cadena de suministro dentro del sistema de las Naciones Unidas. Experiencia relevante a nivel país, particularmente en contextos de desarrollo, entornos frágiles y situaciones humanitarias. Para cada infancia, demuestras... Los Valores Fundamentales de UNICEF: Cuidado, Respeto, Integridad, Confianza, Responsabilidad y Sostenibilidad (CRITAS) sustentan lo que hacemos y la forma en que lo hacemos. Te invitamos a conocer nuestra Carta de Valores: Valores de UNICEF. Las competencias de UNICEF requeridas para este puesto son: (1) Demuestra autoconciencia y conciencia ética (1) (2) Trabaja colaborativamente con otras personas (1) (3) Construye y mantiene alianzas (1) (4) Innova y adopta el cambio (1) (5) Piensa y actúa estratégicamente (1) (6) Impulso para lograr resultados de impacto (1) (7) Gestiona la ambigüedad y la complejidad (1) Familiarízate con nuestro marco de competencias y sus distintos niveles. UNICEF promueve y defiende la protección de los derechos de cada niño y niña, en todas partes y en todo lo que hace, y está mandatado a apoyar la realización de los derechos de todos los niños y ñinas, incluyendo a los más desfavorecidos. Nuestra fuerza laboral global debe reflejar la diversidad de esos niños y ñiñas. La familia de UNICEF está comprometida con la inclusión de todas las personas, independientemente de su raza/origen étnico, discapacidad, identidad de género, orientación sexual, religión, nacionalidad, origen socioeconómico, condición de minoría u otra condición. UNICEF alienta las solicitudes de todas las personas candidatas calificadas, sin importar su género, nacionalidad, origen religioso o étnico, y de personas con discapacidad, incluyendo la neurodivergencia. Ofrecemos una amplia gama de beneficios a nuestro personal, incluyendo licencia parental remunerada, pausas para lactancia y ajustes razonables para personas con discapacidad. UNICEF proporciona ajustes razonables durante todo el proceso de selección. Si necesitas algún ajuste, por favor envía tu solicitud a través del botón de accesibilidad disponible en la página de carreras de UNICEF. Si eres preseleccionado/a, ponte en contacto directamente con la persona reclutadora para compartir más detalles y permitirnos realizar los ajustes necesarios con antelación. UNICEF no contrata a candidatos/as que estén casados con menores de edad (personas menores de 18 años). UNICEF tiene una política de tolerancia cero frente a conductas incompatibles con los objetivos y principios de las Naciones Unidas y UNICEF, incluyendo la explotación y el abuso sexual, el acoso sexual, el abuso de autoridad y la discriminación por motivos de género, nacionalidad, edad, raza, orientación sexual, origen religioso o étnico, o discapacidad. UNICEF está comprometido con la promoción de la protección y salvaguarda de todos los niños y niñas. Por ello, todos los/as candidatos/as seleccionados/as serán sometidos/as a rigurosas verificaciones de referencias y antecedentes, y se espera que cumplan con estos estándares y principios. Las verificaciones incluirán la validación de credenciales académicas y del historial laboral. Es posible que se solicite información adicional para realizar dichas verificaciones, y a los/as candidatos/as seleccionados/as con discapacidad se les podrá pedir, de forma confidencial, documentación de respaldo. Las asignaciones en UNICEF están sujetas a autorización médica. Para puestos internacionales, se requiere la emisión de una visa por parte del país anfitrión del lugar de destino, que será facilitada por UNICEF. Las asignaciones también están condicionadas a la disposición de las personas seleccionadas para cumplir con los requisitos de vacunación vigentes o futuros, en caso de que UNICEF los establezca como obligatorios para su personal. El incumplimiento de dichos requisitos, cuando sean aplicables y en ausencia de una exención médica debidamente aprobada por la autoridad competente de las Naciones Unidas, dará lugar a la cancelación del proceso de selección o podrá dar lugar a otras medidas administrativas, incluida la separación del servicio. De conformidad con el artículo 101, párrafo 3, de la Carta de las Naciones Unidas, la consideración primordial en la contratación del personal es la necesidad de garantizar los más altos estándares de eficiencia, competencia e integridad. UNICEF está comprometido con el fomento de una fuerza laboral inclusiva, representativa y acogedora. Para este puesto, se invita a postular a los/as candidatos/as elegibles y adecuados independientemente de su raza/origen étnico, discapacidad, identidad de género, orientación sexual, religión, nacionalidad, origen socioeconómico, condición de minoría u otra condición. Los/as funcionarios/as gubernamentales que sean considerados/as para empleo en UNICEF normalmente deben renunciar a sus cargos públicos antes de asumir una asignación en la organización.
